elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: The general consent requirement applies, and no consent-free affiliate-assignment exception is provided; defining Customer to include Affiliates does not create such an assignment right.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: Section 22.4(a) permits assignment to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all Customer assets without M&I's consent, subject to notice and Section 21.11.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: Section 22.4(b) permits M&I to assign without Customer consent in connection with a merger, corporate reorganization, or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, stock, or securities.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: For assignments requiring consent, the clause states that the other party's prior written consent shall not be unreasonably withheld.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no prohibition on assignment by M&I to a Customer competitor.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: Upon Customer's change of control, M&I expressly agrees to continue providing Services, subject to stated scope and volume limits; no termination right is granted.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: Customer may assign to an expressly identified successor in the listed transactions, and M&I may assign in connection with a merger, reorganization, or sale of all or substantially all assets, which permits a successor assignment.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: The phrase "in each case upon written notice to the other party" applies to both parties' transaction-based assignment exceptions.
M&I's consent-free exception is not limited to assignment to a successor; it broadly covers assignments "in connection with" a corporate reorganization or sale of assets, stock, or securities.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The general rule requires prior written consent and expressly provides that such consent shall not be unreasonably withheld.
